Untrusted source: inject_data_ue_store is the .write fops of the EDAC debugfs file 'inject_ue' (xddr_inject_ue_fops .write at line 881-885, created by edac_debugfs_create_file("inject_ue", 0200, ...) at lines 907-910), so count and buffer contents come from a write(2) syscall. Violated invariant (validated length equals the index actually used): line 854 declares 'char buf[6], *pbuf, *token[2];' and line 859 clamps 'len = min_t(size_t, count, sizeof(buf))' WITHOUT -1, so len can equal sizeof(buf) == 6; line 863 then writes 'buf[len] = '\0'' at index 6, one byte past the end of the 6-byte stack array whenever the user writes count >= 6 (e.g. write(fd, "255,255", 7)). Unsafe use: the terminator write itself is the out-of-bounds store - a deterministic 1-byte NUL stack out-of-bounds WRITE (KASAN stack-out-of-bounds Write of size 1), clobbering the adjacent stack slot; the subsequent strsep/kstrtou8 parsing then runs on the corrupted stack. This is the seed fix primitive (explicit terminator slot) misapplied - the inverse of the seed's missing-terminator OOB read under the same terminator-slot accounting root cause. CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: buf[len]='\0' at 2019 is in-bounds in this snapshot. drivers/scsi/scsi_proc.c:42 defines PROC_BLOCK_SIZE (3*1024)=3072 and proc_scsi_host_write (lines 64-86) rejects count > 3072 (line 71) before copying count bytes into a full PAGE_SIZE (4096) __get_free_page page and passing (page, count) to ->write_info (line 82). len = count <= 3072 < 4096, so buf[len] always lands inside the page allocation; the f005 claim of a page-boundary OOB write at count == PAGE_SIZE is false for this snapshot because PROC_BLOCK_SIZE caps at 3072.

imm_write_info never writes a terminator (no buf[len]=0 anywhere in the function); for the terminator-write-off-by-one branch there is no offending store. Its missing-termination parse issue is recorded under intent i012, not this branch.
ppa_write_info likewise performs no terminator write; no off-by-one terminator store exists in this branch (missing-termination parsing recorded under i012).
'if (count >= PAGE_SIZE) goto out;' (line 102) before buf[count]='\0' on a __get_free_page page: count <= PAGE_SIZE-1, in-bounds.

limitations: The two edac findings are hypotheses backed by literal source structure (clamp without -1, 6-byte array, terminator index 6); no in-kernel KASAN run was executed in this read-only snapshot - the identical s02 pattern was ASan-verified as 'stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1' by f015's harness, but no new harness was built here.

The sweep enumerated terminator writes of the form buf[idx]=0/'\0' with a usercopy (copy_from_user/memdup_user/vmemdup_user/simple_write_to_buffer) within the preceding 25 lines across all s03 .c/.h files (~120 sites inventoried); sites where the usercopy occurs farther away, is hidden inside a helper called from the writer, or where the terminator index is a complex expression (e.g. buf[i++]=0 loops, ptr writes like *p=0) were not all individually line-verified.

Sites whose clamp uses sizeof(buf)-1 or rejects count >= sizeof(buf) were classified safe in bulk from the printed guard lines; the five smackfs temp[count] sites and the hisilicon/rtw89/toshiba/trace families were guard-pattern matched but not every one deep-read.

The wd33c93 resolution establishes buf[len] in-bounds for this snapshot's PROC_BLOCK_SIZE=3072; the separate uninitialized-tail parsing (OOB read) behavior of the shared scsi_proc page and the imm/ppa missing-termination parses belong to intents i011/i012, not this terminator-write branch.

Both reported files are debugfs control files (0200 versal, 0644 zynqmp) reachable only with a mounted debugfs and the corresponding Xilinx Zynq/UltraScale+ EDAC driver loaded (CONFIG_EDAC_VERSAL/EDAC_ZYNQMP); the 1-byte NUL OOB write corrupts one adjacent stack byte, so impact beyond KASAN-class stack corruption (return-address/adjacent-variable clobber) is not demonstrated.
